title: Rate limiting on auth endpoints
description: Apply rate limiting to authentication endpoints to prevent brute force attacks. Login should be strictly limited; other auth endpoints more leniently.
acceptanceCriteria: Login endpoint limited to 5 requests per 15 minutes per IP
Register endpoint limited to 10 requests per hour per IP
Password reset limited to 3 requests per hour per IP
Rate limit exceeded returns 429 with Retry-After header
Rate limits reset after the window expires

steps.details: Create server/src/middleware/rateLimit.ts. Export: loginLimiter = rateLimit({ windowMs: 15*60*1000, max: 5, message: { error: 'Too many login attempts, try again later' }, standardHeaders: true, legacyHeaders: false }). registerLimiter = rateLimit({ windowMs: 60*60*1000, max: 10 }). forgotPasswordLimiter = rateLimit({ windowMs: 60*60*1000, max: 3 }).

steps.description: Apply rate limiters to auth routes
steps.details: In auth router: router.post('/login', loginLimiter, loginHandler). router.post('/register', registerLimiter, registerHandler). router.post('/forgot-password', forgotPasswordLimiter, forgotPasswordHandler).
Send 6 POST /api/auth/login requests rapidly — the 6th should return 429. Check response headers for RateLimit-Remaining and Retry-After.

technicalNotes: express-rate-limit uses in-memory store by default — fine for single-instance dev
standardHeaders: true adds RateLimit-Policy header per RFC 6585
